reviewMethod: Codex drafting followed by a separate agent editorial review against complete archived source; not independent legal review.

headings.title: Voluntary-act requirement
headings.reviewNote: Identifies the requirement that liability involve conduct including a voluntary act, not that every movement be voluntary.

headings.title: Meaning of voluntary act
headings.reviewNote: Includes both conscious bodily movement and physically possible omissions; subsection4 separately limits omission-only liability.

headings.title: Possession as a voluntary act
headings.reviewNote: Accounts for knowing acquisition or awareness of control long enough to terminate it; does not call every possession voluntary.

headings.title: Liability based solely on an omission
headings.reviewNote: Keeps the express-offense or legally-imposed-duty conditions in the source; distinguishes the definition in subsection2.

entries.reviewSummary: Separate Codex editorial pass against the full archived version and notes: Read voluntary-act requirement, movement/omission definition, knowing possession/control timing and law-imposed duty for sole omission liability. Labels preserve the distinct qualifications rather than declaring all omissions criminal. This is not independent legal review.

headings.title: Attempt, purpose, and substantial steps
headings.reviewNote: Covers purpose, conduct and the substantial-step definition without supplying elements of particular attempted offenses.

headings.title: Impossibility defense and believed circumstances
headings.reviewNote: Preserves the qualification concerning circumstances as the actor believed them; does not assert that impossibility is always irrelevant.

headings.title: Classification of attempted offenses
headings.reviewNote: Keeps the offense-statute exception to lower classification; does not announce an unconditional reduction.

entries.reviewSummary: Separate Codex editorial pass against the full archived version and notes: Read purpose/substantial-step test, factual/legal impossibility qualified by believed circumstances, and one-class-lower default subject to offense-statute exceptions. Headings do not imply impossibility always defeats prosecution. This is not independent legal review.

headings.title: Conspiracy agreements and acts in furtherance
headings.reviewNote: Includes the specified felony classes, agreement and furtherance act. Does not repair the unusual exceeds-ten-years-or-more source wording.

headings.title: Unknown identities of other conspirators
headings.reviewNote: Preserves knowledge of the linked conspiracy as a condition; does not generalize to all unknown participants.

headings.title: Multiple offenses under one conspiracy agreement
headings.reviewNote: Distinguishes the single conspiracy conviction rule from liability for the underlying offenses.

headings.title: Renunciation and raising the issue
headings.reviewNote: Revised generic defendant burden wording to reflect the specified burden of injecting the issue, without implying a burden of proving renunciation; prevention and renunciation conditions remain in body.

headings.title: Conspiracy termination for prosecution time limits
headings.reviewNote: Includes completed objectives, collective abandonment, and conditions for individual termination; no generic limitations period supplied.

headings.title: Conspiracy offense classification
headings.reviewNote: Describes the class-C classification without adding a sentence or merging attempt penalties.

entries.reviewSummary: Separate Codex editorial pass against the full archived version and notes: Read limited felony scope and act in furtherance, unknown identities, single-agreement offenses, prevention-based renunciation and continuing-conspiracy termination rules. Source exceeds ten years or more wording retained without resolving it. Renunciation label revised to distinguish injecting the issue from a burden of proving the defense. This is not independent legal review.

headings.title: Mental-state requirement and statutory exception
headings.reviewNote: Keeps 562.026 and offense-specific mental-state/element requirements; not a claim that all offenses require intent.

headings.title: Meaning of acting purposely
headings.reviewNote: Describes conscious-object definition for conduct or results.

headings.title: Meaning of acting knowingly
headings.reviewNote: Read both subdivisions on awareness of conduct/circumstances and practical certainty of a result.

headings.title: Meaning of acting recklessly
headings.reviewNote: Preserves conscious disregard, substantial/unjustifiable risk and gross deviation requirements.

headings.title: Meaning of criminal negligence
headings.reviewNote: Distinguishes failure to perceive risk from the conscious disregard in subsection4; preserves gross deviation requirement.

entries.reviewSummary: Separate Codex editorial pass against the full archived version and notes: Read statutory mental-state exception and all four mental states, preserving conscious disregard versus failure to perceive risk and conduct/circumstances/result distinctions. This is not independent legal review.

headings.title: Mental states prescribed without identifying particular elements
headings.reviewNote: Concerns a prescribed mental state whose application to elements is unspecified, not an offense omitting a mental state altogether.

headings.title: Requirements prescribed for particular offense elements
headings.reviewNote: Describes the specified-element rule and its treatment of other elements; distinct from subsection1.

headings.title: Offenses without an express mental-state requirement
headings.reviewNote: Keeps both cross-referenced exceptions and the purpose/knowledge standard, rather than implying any culpability suffices.

headings.title: Satisfying mental-state requirements with higher culpability
headings.reviewNote: Describes only the stated substitutions among negligence, recklessness, knowledge and purpose; does not invent new mental states.

headings.title: Knowledge of the offense-defining law
headings.reviewNote: Covers the general non-element rule and express statutory exception without saying ignorance always excuses conduct.

entries.reviewSummary: Separate Codex editorial pass against the full archived version and notes: Read element-specific allocation, default purpose/knowledge with express exclusions, higher-state substitution and absence of required knowledge of law unless statute provides otherwise. This is not independent legal review.

headings.title: Mistakes affecting the required mental state
headings.reviewNote: Includes mistakes of fact or law and the requirement that they negate the required state; not a broad mistake defense.

headings.title: Unpublished rules and official statements of law
headings.reviewNote: Official statements may later be found invalid or erroneous; official law could suggest the statement is valid law. Reasonable reliance and due-diligence qualifications remain in the source.

headings.title: Defendant’s burden to raise reasonable-belief exceptions
headings.reviewNote: Names burden of injecting the specified subsection2 issues, not a general burden to disprove guilt.

entries.reviewSummary: Separate Codex editorial pass against the full archived version and notes: Read mistake negating required mental state, reasonable unpublished-rule/due-diligence and official-statement reliance exceptions, and defendant burden of injecting issue. Raise wording does not convert it to proof. This is not independent legal review. Rechecked subsection 2 and clarified that reliance concerns official statements of law, including statements later found invalid or erroneous.

headings.title: Grounds for responsibility for another’s conduct
headings.reviewNote: Includes express statutory responsibility and purposeful assistance/agreement/attempt to aid before or during the offense; not mere presence.

headings.title: Exceptions to responsibility for another’s conduct
headings.reviewNote: Read victim, necessarily-incident conduct/separate-offense, and abandonment-with-warning-or-prevention exceptions. No broad immunity claimed.

headings.title: Abandonment as an affirmative defense
headings.reviewNote: Refers specifically to subsection2(3), not all exceptions. Read the source annotation on aiding another despite inability to commit the offense individually.

entries.reviewSummary: Separate Codex editorial pass against the full archived version and notes: Read statute-based or purposeful assistance responsibility, victim/necessarily-incidental/abandonment exceptions, related separate offense and affirmative-defense designation for abandonment. Historical aiding-rape case note read without turning it into a general title rule. This is not independent legal review.

headings.title: Corporate criminal liability
headings.reviewNote: Covers omitted duties, qualified agent conduct and management authorization/tolerance as separate statutory grounds.

headings.title: Unincorporated association criminal liability
headings.reviewNote: Keeps this subsection distinct from corporations and preserves legislative-intent and agency conditions.

headings.title: Meaning of agent and high managerial agent
headings.reviewNote: Both section-specific definitions covered; no broader employment-law definition inferred.

entries.reviewSummary: Separate Codex editorial pass against the full archived version and notes: Read corporate omission/agency/high-manager liability separately from narrower unincorporated association grounds, plus agent definitions; titles do not erase scope-of-employment/on-behalf requirements. This is not independent legal review.

headings.title: Entrapment and criminal responsibility
headings.reviewNote: Names the defense topic without assuming it applies in the physical-injury circumstances excluded by subsection3.

headings.title: Meaning of entrapment
headings.reviewNote: Preserves officer/cooperator role, evidence-gathering purpose, inducement and lack of readiness/willingness.

headings.title: Injury or danger to others: entrapment exception
headings.reviewNote: Includes both causing injury and risk of injury to someone other than the entrapment perpetrator; not limited to actual injury.

headings.title: Defendant’s burden to raise entrapment
headings.reviewNote: Uses raise for injecting the issue, not a claim about the ultimate burden of proving every element.

entries.reviewSummary: Separate Codex editorial pass against the full archived version and notes: Read officer/cooperator inducement with lack of readiness/willingness, physical-injury danger exception and burden of injecting issue. Source perpetuated spelling retained; no proof burden inferred. This is not independent legal review.

headings.title: Duress as an affirmative defense
headings.reviewNote: Includes force/threat imminence, unlawfulness, third persons and reasonable firmness; not any kind of pressure.

headings.title: Offenses and circumstances excluding the duress defense
headings.reviewNote: Covers murder and reckless exposure to coercion. Read the felony-murder annotation; no broader case-law conclusion added.

entries.reviewSummary: Separate Codex editorial pass against the full archived version and notes: Read reasonable-firmness/imminent unlawful force affirmative defense and murder/reckless-self-placement exceptions. First-degree felony-murder annotation retained and consistent with exception topic. This is not independent legal review.

headings.title: Intoxication, incapacity, and criminal responsibility
headings.reviewNote: Keeps both involuntariness and specified incapacity in the exception; does not suggest voluntary intoxication negates responsibility.

headings.title: Defendant’s burden to raise intoxication
headings.reviewNote: Describes the issue-injection burden while retaining the conditions elsewhere in the section.

headings.title: Voluntary intoxication evidence and jury instructions
headings.reviewNote: Distinguishes relevant conduct evidence from use to negate an element mental state and includes the jury-instruction requirement.

entries.reviewSummary: Separate Codex editorial pass against the full archived version and notes: Read involuntary incapacity exception, burden of injecting intoxicated/drugged condition and voluntary evidence allowed for relevant conduct but never negating mental state, with required jury instruction. This is not independent legal review.

headings.title: Mental disease or defect and criminal responsibility
headings.reviewNote: Preserves incapacity at the time of conduct and the statutory knowing/appreciating standard; not a blanket exemption for diagnoses.

headings.title: Defense procedures under chapter 552
headings.reviewNote: Retains the exact procedural cross-reference without inventing procedures or burdens.

entries.reviewSummary: Separate Codex editorial pass against the full archived version and notes: Read mental-disease/defect incapacity at time of conduct and referral of defense procedures to chapter552; headings avoid diagnosing or broadening eligibility. This is not independent legal review.
